title: Explicit dynamics: free fall
sentence: An unconstrained block under gravity, integrated by central differences — explicit dynamics checked against a schoolbook drop.
theory: Central differences advance $\mathbf{M}\ddot{\mathbf{u}} = \mathbf{f}_{ext} - \mathbf{f}_{int}$ with a lumped $\mathbf{M}$, so each step costs one matrix-free force pass and no factorisation. Stability needs $\Delta t \le \dfrac{L_e}{c}$ with $c = \sqrt{E/\rho}$ (the Courant condition); `dtFactor` is the safety margin on the Irons estimate. For a constant acceleration the leapfrog is exact, so after $t$ the block has fallen $u = \tfrac{1}{2}gt^2 = 4.905\,\mathrm{\mu m}$.
